messages:
alejandro: Customer reports intermittent 400 from /v1/embeddings when sending batched requests (>1 item). Happens ~10% of the time, non-deterministic. They see an error like: "invalid_input: embedding dimension mismatch". I asked for request IDs and they supplied some—posting them below. Need a quick repro checklist to hand back and a request for a debug bundle.

maya: Thanks. Can you paste the exact request IDs, the model name the customer is calling, and one full curl they used (with any headers redacted)? Also ask them to try single-item calls to check if batching triggers it.

alejandro: Request IDs: req_0acb1f2e, req_7f3d9a4c, req_22b01eaa. Model: rwd-embed-1536. Sample (redacted) curl they sent: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-embed-1536","input":[[0.1,0.2,...],[0.3,0.4,...]]}'
```
They also mentioned sometimes they gzip the payload and saw a 400 only when gzip is on.

ryan: I pulled the runtime logs for those req ids. There's a pattern: our batcher merges two in-flight requests and sends a shaped payload to the model runner. Example log snippet (sanitized): 
```
[2026-03-10T14:12:03Z] batcher: merged batches sizes [1,7] -> combined shape [8,1536]
[2026-03-10T14:12:03Z] decoder: client_payload_shape=[8,1537] -> reject invalid_input: embedding_dim=1537 expected=1536 (req=req_0acb1f2e)
```
So at least one client payload had an extra element. Could be off-by-one in client-side serialization or an accidental nested array.

julie: Two quick checks: 1) confirm the customer is calling the model variant they think (quantized variants can have different postproc). 2) Have them print the length of each embedding vector before sending (e.g., in Python len(vec) for each item). Also try forcing an explicit shape by sending a single item: `-d '{"model":"rwd-embed-1536","input":[[0.1,0.2,...]]}'` — if single-item always works it's likely a batching merge edge case.

alejandro: I asked the customer to run a tiny repro. They sent back a minimal failing example — turned out they were accidentally sending a nested wrapper for singletons. Bad payload: 
```
# failing
{"model":"rwd-embed-1536","input":[[[0.1,0.2,...]]]}  # note double nesting
```
Fixed payload: 
```
# working
{"model":"rwd-embed-1536","input":[[0.1,0.2,...]]}
```
When they gzip the double-nested payload we hit the 400 during merge more often. So this explains intermittent behavior.

ops-oncall: Good catch. For completeness collect a debug bundle from the customer's session so eng-runtime can correlate traces. Ask customer to add header `X-Debug-Trace: true` and re-run the failing request; then run: 
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/internal/debug/bundle?trace_id=<the X-Trace header value> -o dbg.tgz
```
If they can't create the bundle, ask for the exact curl they used and the raw request body (or a redacted version) plus the request ids. If they hit 401 while fetching bundle that's likely ephemeral token expiry — tell them to use the same token used for the request.

support-bot: debug bundle created: dbg-2026-03-10-1958765432-req0acb.tgz (size=4.1MB) for trace_id=trace_1958765432. Uploaded to internal ticket.

maya: Next steps: 1) Eng-runtime (ryan) — can you confirm whether we should hard-validate client payload shapes earlier and return a clearer error? 2) DevEx -> update docs to call out double-nest gotcha in quickstart embedding examples, and mention gzip caveat. 3) Support -> advise the customer to validate vec lengths client-side and share the debug bundle.

ryan: We'll add an early sanity check in the request deserializer to validate input vectors are all length 1536 and return a specific error like `invalid_input: expected embedding dim 1536 but got N` before batching. I'll open a small PR and backfill a test for nested arrays.

alejandro: I'll send the guidance to the customer (single-item test, check vec len, how to produce debug bundle) and attach the bundle to the internal ticket. Will update here once customer verifies. :thumbsup:
